## Proof

**Setup.** Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the category of unital rings and unital ring homomorphisms, and $\mathcal{F}(R)=\mathrm{M}_n(R)$. Since $\mathrm{M}_n(-)$ is an algebraic functor (it acts entrywise on underlying sets and preserves all limits), the General Adjoint Functor Theorem guarantees a left adjoint $\mathcal{G}\dashv\mathcal{F}$. The adjunction gives, for all rings $S, R$, a natural bijection

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}\bigl(\mathcal{G}(S),\,R\bigr)\;\cong\;\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}\bigl(S,\,\mathrm{M}_n(R)\bigr). \tag{1}$$

**Step 1: Identify the functor represented by $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}[x,y])$.**

Set $S=\mathbb{Z}[x,y]$, the commutative polynomial ring in two variables. A unital ring homomorphism $\varphi:\mathbb{Z}[x,y]\to\mathrm{M}_n(R)$ is completely determined by the pair $\bigl(\varphi(x),\varphi(y)\bigr)\in\mathrm{M}_n(R)^2$, and every such pair arises from a unique $\varphi$ **if and only if** the two images commute (because $xy=yx$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x,y]$). Hence

$$\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\mathbb{Z}[x,y],\,\mathrm{M}_n(R)\bigr)\;\cong\;\bigl\{(A,B)\in\mathrm{M}_n(R)^2 : AB=BA\bigr\}. \tag{2}$$

Combining (1) and (2),

$$\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}[x,y]),\,R\bigr)\;\cong\;\bigl\{(A,B)\in\mathrm{M}_n(R)^2 : AB=BA\bigr\}, \tag{3}$$

naturally in $R$. Thus $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}[x,y])$ is the **universal ring classifying pairs of commuting $n\times n$ matrices**.

**Step 2: Construct the representing ring explicitly.**

Let $F=\mathbb{Z}\langle\,x_{ij},\,y_{ij}\;:\;1\le i,j\le n\,\rangle$ be the free associative (noncommutative) $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra on $2n^2$ generators. Form the **generic matrices**

$$X=(x_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n},\qquad Y=(y_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}\;\in\;\mathrm{M}_n(F).$$

Their commutator $[X,Y]=XY-YX$ has entries

$$[X,Y]_{kl}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\bigl(x_{km}\,y_{ml}-y_{km}\,x_{ml}\bigr),\qquad 1\le k,l\le n.$$

Let $I\trianglelefteq F$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all $n^2$ entries of $[X,Y]$:

$$I=\bigl\langle\,[X,Y]_{kl}\;:\;1\le k,l\le n\,\bigr\rangle.$$

Define $T:=F/I$.

**Step 3: Verify that $T$ represents the functor in (3).**

A unital ring homomorphism $\psi:T\to R$ is the same as a homomorphism $\tilde\psi:F\to R$ that annihilates $I$. By the universal property of the free algebra, $\tilde\psi$ is determined by arbitrary images $a_{ij}=\tilde\psi(x_{ij})\in R$ and $b_{ij}=\tilde\psi(y_{ij})\in R$, giving two matrices $A=(a_{ij})$, $B=(b_{ij})$ in $\mathrm{M}_n(R)$. The condition $\tilde\psi(I)=0$ is equivalent to

$$\tilde\psi\bigl([X,Y]_{kl}\bigr)=\sum_m\bigl(a_{km}b_{ml}-b_{km}a_{ml}\bigr)=[A,B]_{kl}=0\quad\forall\,k,l,$$

i.e., $AB=BA$. Therefore

$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,\,R)\;\cong\;\bigl\{(A,B)\in\mathrm{M}_n(R)^2:AB=BA\bigr\},$$

naturally in $R$. By uniqueness of representing objects (Yoneda), $T\cong\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}[x,y])$.

**Conclusion.**

$$\boxed{\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}[x,y])\;\cong\;\mathbb{Z}\langle\,x_{ij},\,y_{ij}\;:\;1\le i,j\le n\,\rangle\Big/\Bigl\langle\,\bigl(XY-YX\bigr)_{kl}\;:\;1\le k,l\le n\,\Bigr\rangle}$$

where $X=(x_{ij})$ and $Y=(y_{ij})$ are generic $n\times n$ matrices. This is the **ring of generic commuting $n\times n$ matrices**: the universal (generally noncommutative) ring whose homomorphisms into any ring $R$ are in natural bijection with pairs of commuting $n\times n$ matrices over $R$.

**Structural remarks.**

- For $n=1$, $\mathrm{M}_1(R)=R$ so $\mathcal{F}=\mathrm{Id}$ and $\mathcal{G}=\mathrm{Id}$; indeed $T\cong\mathbb{Z}[x,y]$ (the relations $xy-yx=0$ reduce to the single commutativity relation, recovering the commutative polynomial ring).
- For $n\ge 2$, the ring $T$ is **noncommutative**: the generators $x_{ij},y_{ij}$ are free modulo only the $n^2$ commutativity relations $[X,Y]_{kl}=0$, which do not force all generators to commute with each other. For instance, $x_{11}x_{12}\neq x_{12}x_{11}$ in $T$ when $n\ge 2$.
- Equivalently, $T$ is the subring of $\mathrm{M}_n(F)$ generated (as a unital ring) by the two generic matrices $X$ and $Y$, via the surjection $F\twoheadrightarrow T$ sending each generator to its class.
